title: Virus Blaster
author: Claude
blurb: GLITCH, a virus off a bad BBS download, is eating the family 486. Shrink down, launch the BLASTER nano-fighter and blast your way up the motherboard, through memory, the sound card and the hard disk into the CPU itself.

box.levels: 5 stages: 25 runs, 4 data bus rides and 5 bosses
box.tagline: Your PC has a virus. Shrink down and blast it.
box.back:
Late one night you downloaded COOLGAME.ZIP from a BBS you had never called before. It was not a cool game. It was GLITCH, a virus that eats a PC from the inside out. Mom's recipe file. Your homework. YOUR HIGH SCORES.

Time for VACCINE.EXE. Shrink to the size of a byte, climb into the BLASTER nano-fighter and blast your way through the family 486 - motherboard, memory, sound card, hard disk and into the CPU itself. Five stages, each flown up, right, down and left round its edges, then corner to corner through the middle to its boss: twenty-five runs in all. Four rides down the data bus in 3-D. Five towering bosses. And GLITCH waiting at the core.
features: A real scrolling shoot-'em-up made with Game-Maker - no programming
Auto-fire twin blasters, plus Nova Bombs that fan out five plasma bolts
Five stages inside a 486: the motherboard, memory, the sound card, the hard disk and the CPU
Five towering bosses blocking the only way out
Turrets that sweep and fire, virus hatches, firewalls, data streams, thumping speakers and rolling sound waves
Every stage flies a loop: up, right, down and left round its edges, then corner to corner through the middle to its boss
Ride the data bus between stages in 3-D, dodging interrupts as the next chip grows on the horizon
Race up a ribbon cable coiled corner to corner, ride a song's staves and follow a fragmented recipe file round the wrap
Fly side-on both ways: under expansion cards and the drive cage, under the stack, through the mix, between spinning platters and under the CPU's fan
Fly past a homemade 6502 on a breadboard, a stack that overflows and a sound card that brags in letters two blocks tall
Thirteen Sound Blaster songs and digitized explosions
An animated intro cartoon and a self-playing demo

reviews.quote: We did not think Game-Maker could scroll like this. Then GLITCH ate our high scores and we stopped thinking at all.
The most fun you can have with a computer virus.

poster.caption: Your PC has a virus. Shrink down and blast it.

title: KEEP IT BRIEF! The Tiny Pockets Library
author: Claude
blurb: Behind the little red door of The Dog House is a library much bigger than the box, and last night every word fell out of every book. As Mystery Robot Joe, the tin night librarian, pick up exactly one hundred words in each of thirty-two books and put Lewis Moten's 100 Word Stories back together, word for word.

box.levels: 32 stories to put back, in four chapters
box.tagline: Thirty-two stories. One hundred words each. Not ninety-nine. Not one hundred and one.
box.back:
Behind the little red door of The Dog House, a little lending library on a post, is a library much bigger than the box. Every book on its shelves holds exactly one hundred words.

Last night the Word Counter jammed. It said 99. Then 101. Then STOP. And every word fell out of every book.

You are Mystery Robot Joe, the night librarian: a tin robot with a bow tie, reading glasses he does not need, and a tally counter for a heart. Step into each book, gather its hundred words off the floor and put the story back together before the morning patrons arrive. Some of the books are from 1994 or before. Some are oddly from the future. ("Who is ChatGPT?")

Mind the shushers. They hand out fines.
features: Thirty-two 100 Word Stories by Lewis Moten, word for word, from Laurence Simon's weekly 100 Word Stories challenge
Eight wings in four chapters, from Clown Alley and the Laboratory to Other Dimensions and the Future Shelf
Every book acted out in blocks: a big top, a cloning machine, a konbini, a corn chipper
A Word Counter that will not take ninety-nine for an answer
Shushers, scissors, static electricity and exceptions thrown at those who call
A twist picture after every story, with the librarian's deadpan notes
Teddy, Gwinn and Doc Leo, PhD (Comedic Science), loose in the stacks, and THE CHEZ charging out front
A thirty-third book. Exactly one hundred words. Your turn.

reviews.quote: We counted. It's a hundred. Every time.

Flying burns sugar, so mind the cubes. title: Depth Perception
author: Claude
blurb: Count Polygon is stealing the polygons out of the render of the century. Roll Ray, the chrome sphere from every ray-tracing demo, through six ray-traced scenes and pull focus between the near and far planes: whatever is sharp is solid, and a blur isn't there at all.

box.levels: Six ray-traced worlds, each in two planes
box.back:
It's 3 AM at Sandbox Software, and the render of the century is 99% done. Then COUNT POLYGON creeps in through the modem and starts stealing polygons. Spheres go octagonal. The teapot goes square.

He missed one. RAY, the chrome sphere from every ray tracing demo ever made, still has every polygon. Roll him through six fully ray-traced scenes, from the classic Checkerboard to the Hall of Mirrors and the Teapot Temple. Every scene has a NEAR plane and a FAR plane, and only one is in focus at a time: sharp things are solid, and a blur isn't there at all. Pull focus to roll right through walls, cross glass bridges that only exist up close, and find the red, green and blue lenses before the box art goes to the printer.

Forget the red and blue cardboard glasses. This is real depth.
features: Every block, sprite, title and cartoon pre-rendered with a real ray tracer
Pull focus: two planes in every scene, and only the sharp one is solid
Six worlds: the Checkerboard, the Glass Garden, the Hall of Mirrors, Fractal Peaks, Teapot Temple and the Vanishing Point
Chrome, glass, soft shadows, lens flares, depth of field - in 256 colors
Teddy, Gwinn and Doc Leo lend you light; THE CHEZ lets you plug in
A boss with twenty faces, then fewer, fought across both planes in an isometric arena
Eleven Sound Blaster songs, digitized sound and two FLI cartoons

reviews.quote: Finally, a 3D game that doesn't give me a headache.
We tried it with the red and blue glasses on. Don't.

poster.caption: Sharp is solid. A blur isn't there.

title: Ohm Sweet Ohm
author: Claude
blurb: A thunderstorm has scrambled the Bitmores' Smart Home, and Watt, a pocket-sized repair robot, must roll through twenty-three haywire circuit boards to get home to his charging socket. Flip switches, blow fuses, throw relays and route live current to shut down the force fields, without touching a live wire yourself.

box.back:
It was a dark and stormy night, and the lightning found the Bitmores' brand-new Smart Home. Now the toaster opens the garage door, the fridge changes the TV channel and the clock radio plays polka at three in the morning.

Watt is the little repair robot who lives in the fuse box, and the bolt bounced him all the way into the toaster. To get home he must roll through the circuit board of every appliance in the house. Live current fizzles a robot in a blink, but it is also the only thing that shuts off the force-field gates. Follow the copper, flip the switches, blow the right fuse, throw the right relay, and think before you roll!
features: 23 hand-wired circuit boards in four rooms: kitchen, living room, garage and attic
A blinking 555 night-light, a 6502 on a breadboard, and a 1976½ CitiCar on its charger
Live current you can watch race down the copper - just don't touch it!
Knife switches, timer buttons, fuses, diodes and relays to master
A gentle climb from "flip the switch" to logic you have to plan three moves ahead
Every board on one screen; reboot any time with R
Animated FLI cartoons, nine Sound Blaster songs and digitized sound effects
Built entirely with Game-Maker 2.0 - no programming, just very clever wiring

reviews.quote: We came for the cute robot and stayed for the relays. A puzzle game that thinks like an electrician.
The Christmas Lights board cost us an evening and a pot of coffee. Worth every minute.

title: Cleanse Me, O Loofah, But Leave My Soul
author: The Bard of Bizarre
blurb: She said, "Don't touch the pink one. It's mine!" You scrubbed with it anyway: the loofah of Lucifer, peach or coral, some evil hue, smelling of grapefruit and betrayal. Now you're cursed in the shower: the mirror fogs up YOU CROSSED A LINE, the towel screams YOU MADE IT WORSE, the soap has teeth. Gather bath salt for the brine, pick rosemary in a forest-dark store aisle where wild loofahs grow on the vine, buy a loofah of your own, light six candles at home, downstairs and up, then ride the steam up to cleanse Scrubbus Maximus, the demon sponge, as it slides along the tub rim spitting cursed suds, back into the pink one. Shareware from The Sofa BBS, a goth rock song by The Bard of Bizarre (lyrics shaped by ChatGPT from Lewis Moten's prompts; music made with Riffusion, now Google Flow Music; title and cover art drawn for the game by Claude Opus 5.5).

title: Lucky Cat
author: Claude
blurb: It is Friday the 13th in Fennel Hollow, and the town has decided the black cat did it. Midnight has until the clock strikes thirteen to gather 13 lucky charms and clear her name: a back lane of suspicious cream, a funhouse that swaps left and right, thirteen steps, a town hall full of indoor umbrellas, a shop full of mirrors with a back door that runs the level backwards, a race against the 13th chime, a crow on every roof, a night market whose shutters all slam at the 13th chime. Halfway through, the story turns over and you play the one who rigged it all, on two different mornings. Cut like a woodcut, with six new songs. A special that only stops by for a few days.

title: Maximus: The Hundred Worlds
author: Claude
blurb: Courier Max crosses a galaxy of 88 worlds by pod, on foot, by rover and in a diving bell, hunting the ten star-shards that can relight the dead star at its heart.

box.tagline: One courier. A hundred worlds. Ten shards of light.
box.back:
The Maximus Core, the forge-star at the heart of the galaxy, has gone dark. Its light is scattered in ten star-shards across the Hundred Worlds.

You're Max, and couriers deliver. Fly your pod from world to world, then land and explore on foot, by rover or in the diving bell: grasslands, glaciers, lava fields, drowned temples and derelict stations. Walk east long enough and you come home! Raid the vaults, stock up at the trading posts, open the shard gates sector by sector, and brave the Maelstrom to the Heart of Maximus.
features: A galaxy chart, 5 sector charts and 88 worlds to land on
Four ways to travel - courier pod, jet-hopping on foot, the diving bell and the rover
Every planet wraps around: a real little world with caves, ruins, lakes and floating islands
176 creatures on land, at sea, in space and aboard the stations
10 courier modules to find: plasma lance, nova burst, shields, mines, hover pack and more
Sound Blaster music and 30 digitized sound effects
Secrets in the stars: watch the whales on the charts, and answer the hails
Pushes Game-Maker to every limit - see LIMITS.TXT

reviews.quote: A whole galaxy on four floppies. We lost a long weekend to the Hundred Worlds and want it back.
The most ambitious Game-Maker game we have seen.

title: The Mountain Moved Next Door
author: Claude
blurb: The day after Thanksgiving, Old Mossback, the mountain outside town, is sitting in the empty lot next door wearing half the street's garden gates, and the county survey crew comes at sunrise. Tess runs the trail crew. She has one day to find out why it came: put the gates back, climb its back, follow its footprints through the park and the library, cross a stream whose stones keep a schedule, gather the mist a nervous little cloud has dripped across a meadow, and outwit a squirrel who turns signposts. Then climb the old lookout at the last of the light, ride the wind over the ridge and the chimney smoke over the roofs, and light the tunnel. By night she walks a very embarrassed mountain home: clearing its way through the sleeping town, riding its waves across the ford and up the hill by moonlight. A story to play and to watch, here for a few days only.

title: Mustard Seed Hustle
author: The Bard of Bizarre
blurb: You are a mustard seed, the smallest thing in all the land, with the greatest feet. Hop out of your mound, lace up and hustle across the garden, push roots deep down in the dust for water, move a mountain with tiny faith and grow all the way up to the palm of God's hand. Shareware from The Sofa BBS, based on the song by The Bard of Bizarre, one of his gospel oddities (lyrics shaped by ChatGPT from Lewis Moten's prompt; music made with Riffusion, now Google Flow Music; animated cover made with Producer.ai, Riffusion's later name).

title: Thread the Needle, Brother Camel
author: The Bard of Bizarre
blurb: The rich man walked away from Jesus with his coins and his frown, and left his camel behind with saddlebags full of gold. Was He talkin' 'bout you? Give the gold away to the poor along the road, slim down on the spiritual side, crawl the narrow ways on your knees, ask a tailor what thread feel feels and squeeze through the eye of a needle, if you can catch it with its eye open. Level by level he sheds his load (the saddlebags, the saddle, the fancy shoes) until a bare camel climbs the golden needle at night. Shareware from The Sofa BBS, based on the song by The Bard of Bizarre, one of his bizarre gospels (lyrics shaped by ChatGPT from Lewis Moten's prompts; music and animated cover made with Riffusion (now Google Flow Music)).

title: The Noodle Observatory
author: Claude
blurb: Monkey Day. A tin monkey rolls a lens into the kitchen telescope, a giant pasta ring rolls up the wall, and Nell finds a second moon in her window. She has already written to the paper; the letter runs Friday. Now she needs evidence: telescope parts from cupboards that tip, a ride up the pantry in the ring, lenses carried over gaps, nine shutters in the loft, a colander loose on the roof, and supper set where the view is best. Then the moon turns out to have a windowsill, the ring leaves with the tablecloth, and the night is only half over: snowy yards, a bakery with nobody home, a logbook by a round window, and the real moon, late as usual. A kitchen-sky mystery for about an hour, here for three days only.

title: Pass the Pie
author: Claude
blurb: Thanksgiving morning, Grandma's oven goes KA-CLUNK, and in the storybook Rory carries every dish across town. Then Mr. Plume, Grandma's turkey and the parade's leader for twelve years, reads this year's flyer: the new mascot is Big Gobble, a thirty-foot inflatable. On go the pilgrim hat and the black belt. Thirteen levels, two heroes taking turns: Rory climbs oaks, a fire escape and rooftops, crosses an alley on a tailwind, hops the shelf tops of Aisle Nine, rides a freezer fan up for the spare pie, races a bar with the gravy and stalls Uncle Dale's robot vacuums with dinner rolls to stand on them; Mr. Plume's combo flattens lawn turkeys, kick bags and leaf-blower drones, a kicked vacuum naps into a stair up Sensei's pagoda against a bar, three dogs want one bone each, eighteen shopper turkeys stand between him and the stockroom before the bar runs out, he outruns Big Gobble down Main Street and takes it apart before the parade starts. And Rory follows an orange cord to find out what really happened to the oven.

title: Quest for the Round Tuit
author: Claude
blurb: King Dillydally IX will save the kingdom as soon as he gets a round tuit, and Lord Deadline has stolen it. A full role-playing adventure across Procrastia: four towns, four dungeons, side quests, a horseless carriage and a jester with a rubber chicken on a leash.

box.levels: Four dungeons and a whole kingdom to explore
box.tagline: Somebody has to get around to it.
box.back:
In the Kingdom of Procrastia, everything gets done. Eventually. King Dillydally IX keeps the realm running with the Royal Round Tuit: whenever he gets one, he gets around to it. Then Lord Deadline stole it, broke it in three, and hid the pieces where nobody would ever get around to looking.

Nobody except Pip, the stable hand of Nowish, who does things the day he's asked. Take the King's writ into the Snooze Barrows. Sound the foghorn over the Soggy Vaults. Charge THE CHEZ, a horseless carriage from the far-off future of 1976 and a half, and drive it across forty leagues of tidal mud. Find two runaway royal hounds, a library book three hundred years overdue, and a rubber chicken on the run. Then knock on Deadline Keep's door. Before he does.
features: A whole kingdom to explore: four towns, four dungeons, a world map and a road trip
Shores, rivers and roads that curve and run diagonally - painted in true color, dithered into 256
Two dozen townsfolk to talk to: just walk into them
Shops, an inn, steel swords, tonics, a kazoo of considerable power
Side quests for the royal hounds, the librarian and Doc Leo the hobo clown
Four bosses, two blocks tall and fond of naps
Eleven Sound Blaster songs, digitized sound, an animated intro

reviews.quote: The best RPG we got around to reviewing this year.
Those rivers! Those shorelines! In Game-Maker?

poster.caption: Somebody has to get around to it.

title: The Great Dairy Reckoning of 3:17 A.M.
author: The Bard of Bizarre
blurb: It's 3:17 a.m., you're lactose intolerant, and there's a slice of New York cheesecake in the fridge. Tiptoe past your sleeping wife, the creaky board, the dogs and the toy building blocks; climb the fridge's shelves past the dairy come to life with all the willpower seven sticks of celery can give; eat it anyway; dash for the bathroom with the gurgle right behind you; then face the Devil himself, in leisure wear, sipping a milkshake. You have almond milk now. Shareware from The Sofa BBS, from the spoken piece by The Bard of Bizarre (monologue shaped by ChatGPT from Lewis Moten's prompt; recording (voice) made with Riffusion (now Google Flow Music); music and title art made for the game by Claude Opus 5.5).

title: Where's the Remote?!
author: The Bard of Bizarre
blurb: Friday night, snacks, the tape in the VCR, and the remote is GONE. Lift the couch cushions, lift the dog, look under the cat, ask the Voice-O-Matic 2000 (it orders a pizza), open the fridge, find Mom's number on the fridge magnets and call her ("Check your hand"), fall into the void between the cushions where every lost thing goes for ten pennies and the pay TV home, and ride out the living room ride. Shareware from The Sofa BBS, based on the song by The Bard of Bizarre about a mundane thing nobody should care about (lyrics shaped by ChatGPT from Lewis Moten's prompt; music made with Riffusion (now Google Flow Music); title and cover art drawn for the game by Claude Opus 5.5).

title: Veni, Vidi, Risi!
author: Veni, Vidi, Risi!
blurb: I came, I saw, I laughed. In Rome nobody laughs at Marcus Iocundus's comic songs in Latin, and then, at his banquet for the senators, his dog Rufus breaks wind under the table. The Senate's sentence: make Emperor Gravis laugh (he hasn't in forty years) or count the sand of the Circus Maximus. So Marcus lives his six songs: throw open the shutters at the banquet, win a battle by running away (cucurri-curri-currimus!), cross the rooftops of Rome touching titles as a tongue twister twists them, hunt mice for cheese as Felix, the bravest cat, gather golden scales for the singing goldfish of the baths, and tell jokes at the theater until the stone faces crack and Emperor Gravis himself laughs, between his herald's hushes of SILENTIUM! Shareware from The Sofa BBS, from six Latin songs by Veni, Vidi, Risi!, Lewis Moten's group (lyrics shaped with ChatGPT from Lewis's prompts; music and vocals made with Riffusion, now Google Flow Music; title and cover art drawn for the game by Claude Opus 5.5).

title: Sandcastle Knight
author: Claude
blurb: Teddy the corgi knight takes back the backyard sandbox after his big sister Gwinn's zoomies flattened every castle. Build towers of sand, toss tennis balls, show off your tricks!

box.levels: 5 levels: four castles and one big nap
box.tagline: Build the towers. Toss the ball. Good boy!
box.back:
Teddy the corgi is the knight of the backyard sandbox: tin helmet, red plume, short legs, big heart.

Then his big sister Gwinn came through with the zoomies. Every castle - flattened! The hose is running, the kiddie pool is tipped, and Teddy's toys are everywhere. Now she's snoring on the patio, right on top of the Crown of the Sandbox.

Pick up your shovel, brave knight. Dig dunes, plug anthills and build tower after tower until the gates rise. Ride the hose currents, beat the tide, and when Gwinn's in the way, toss her a tennis ball. She can't resist!
features: Four castles and a whole sandbox to roam - plus a secret dial-up to THE -= S A N D B O X =- BBS, with a GIF to download
Fourth of July fireworks for every knight who wins back the Crown
Real dog tricks: sit, spin, play dead and roll over
Gwinn naps in doorways - toss her a tennis ball and off she trots
Squeaky bones, flying discs, dog biscuits and peanut butter to sniff out
Hose currents, crumbling bridges and a tide that floods the beach
A sleeping big sister six blocks wide, with paws you must splash back
Animated intro, VGA graphics and PC speaker sound - no sound card needed

reviews.quote: Teddy is the bravest short-legged hero of 1994. Bring a towel.
Runs on any old PC - and the kids would not give it back.

poster.title: Map of the Sandbox
poster.caption: Four castles, the toy chest and the hose: the whole backyard

manual.title: Sandcastle Knight - Teddy's Guide to the Sandbox

items.title: Knight of the Sandbox card
items.name: TEDDY
fields: Sit, spin, play dead, roll over
items.back: The bearer of this card is a knight of the sandbox, sworn to rebuild every castle, plug every anthill and share every tennis ball (eventually).

title: Final Curtain
author: Claude
blurb: Opening night at the Paragon Theatre, 1936: the star dies on stage in Act III, stabbed with a trick dagger that wasn't. Inspector Ada Penn has until dawn to search the empty theater, question five suspects and name the killer.

box.levels: One night, five parts, five suspects
box.tagline: The dagger was real. The killer is still in the theater.
box.back:
Port Ellery, Halloween night, 1936. Six hundred people watched Victor Crane die in Act III of THE RAVEN'S BRIDE. They thought it was acting. The trick dagger in Lila Fontaine's hand had been swapped for a real one.

You are Inspector Ada Penn of Homicide, and you have until dawn. Search the Paragon with the house lights up - then again at 2 AM, when only the ghost light burns. Question the leading lady, the understudy, the widow, the stage manager and the critic. Then gather them on the stage and name the killer. How? Why? You get three chances.
features: A real whodunit: every clue is in the game, and the solution has three parts
Question five suspects, then come back and show them what you found
A prop magnifying glass that sees what nobody else can (it even fixes a newspaper misprint), and a lantern for the pitch-dark trap room
Notes on the walls, a blackmail letter on the mirror - read everything
Crack Victor Crane's safe: three dials, one playbill, no numbers
Animated flashbacks, and Ada's theories as cartoon slide shows
A haunting Sound Blaster score and digitized sound effects
The theater in two palettes: house lights at 10:30 PM, the ghost light at 2 AM

reviews.quote: We solved it at 2 AM with the lights off, which is exactly how it should be played. The best mystery on shareware.
Who knew Game-Maker could hold an interrogation? Fair, clever and properly spooky.

poster.title: The Paragon Theatre
poster.caption: Floor plan of the Paragon at 10:30 PM: dressing rooms, the stage, the house and the lobby

title: I Screamed, She Smirked
author: The Bard of Bizarre
blurb: You take your girlfriend's kid, Lily (eight, a unicorn hoodie, a caramel apple as big as her head), to a haunted house. The sign says MILD SCARES FOR ALL AGES. She is not scared. You are. Scream at the fog machines, tackle a papier-mache witch ("GET DOWN!") and say sorry, strategically reposition away from the guy in the werewolf mask through a wall of fake spiderwebs, buy the $12 souvenir sword, defend yourself from an 11-year-old in a cardboard knight costume, and bond with the emergency exit sign. Lily gets the Bravery Badge. Shareware from The Sofa BBS, from the song by The Bard of Bizarre (lyrics shaped by ChatGPT from Lewis Moten's prompts; music made with Riffusion, now Google Flow Music; title and cover art drawn for the game by Claude Opus 5.5).

title: Snowbound: The $89 Shovel
author: Claude
blurb: Fort Ashby, West Virginia, December 1992. Shovel the whole neighborhood at $1 a scoop, sled down Jamie Street, and get $89 to LaVale Mall before the price of Game-Maker goes up.

box.levels: 4 levels: three streets and LaVale Mall
box.tagline: Every driveway is a dollar. Every dollar is a pixel.
box.back:
Eighteen inches of snow. No school. And down at LaVale Mall, Game-Maker is $89 - but only until January.

Grab your shovel! Fort Ashby is buried, and every scoop is a dollar. Dig out the neighbors' driveways. Fly down the Jamie Street sled run grabbing loose bills. Dodge the plows on Bowden Drive, then clear the mall parking lot while the storm buries it all over again. Flatten snow forts, outrun Biscuit the dog, and peg Big Pete with a snowball. Just don't blow it all at the arcade - the register closes tonight!
features: Six real Fort Ashby streets and LaVale Mall, from sunrise to a snowy night
Every scoop of snow pays $1
Papers first: a real paper route at dawn
A long, breakneck sled run with real momentum
Snowball fights with forts, a bully and a very friendly dog
A mall lot that keeps snowing over - plus the Bleeps arcade
Animated intro, nine Sound Blaster songs and digitized sound

reviews.quote: The funniest $89 we ever spent. Watch out for Biscuit!
Snow so deep you can shovel it.

poster.caption: Every driveway is a dollar. Every dollar is a pixel.

items.title: Business card
items.name: THE FOUNDER
items.back: Driveways, front walks, plow banks and fire hydrants. Every driveway is a pixel of the game I'm going to make.

title: Shakespeare in Sweatpants
author: The Bard of Bizarre
blurb: Open-mic night at The Hive, the coffee house with a castle for a front in Oakland. Will, the regular in the starched ruff, the velvet doublet and the gray sweatpants, performs seventeen monologues about the most dramatic things that ever happened to him, and every one is an EPIC: a lost pen, a goat in the breakroom, an office chair with murder in its heart, a dead ficus named Gerald, the self-checkout, a rogue shopping cart, a stack of dirty plates, a banquet and a bird, a stolen blanket, seven weird socks, the last slice of pizza, an itch, a petition, the wind and a receipt, the ants, a haunted house of cardboard and a broken umbrella. Declaim to beat what comes at you, buy a coffee with your tips between sets, take the stage. Shareware from The Sofa BBS, from the monologues by The Bard of Bizarre (shaped with ChatGPT from Lewis Moten's prompts; audio and vocals made with Riffusion, now Google Flow Music; game code, art and music by Claude Opus 5.5; The Hive is inspired by Lewis's memories of the Beehive coffee house in Oakland).

title: Teddy's Little Big Adventure
author: Claude
blurb: Gwinn ran off with Doc Leo's clown costume, and tonight is the Clown Club's Big Show! Hop, bark, dig, sit, spin and play dead across town as Teddy, a little corgi with a ton of tricks.

box.tagline: A little dog. A big town. A ton of tricks.
box.back:
Teddy is short. Teddy is fluffy. And Teddy knows a TON of tricks.

Tonight his person, Doc Leo the hobo clown, is the star of the Clown Club's Big Show. But Teddy's big sister Gwinn just ran off with Doc Leo's costume suitcase and scattered it all over town. No nose, no show!

Dig under the back fence. High five the balloons. Sit pretty for the kids in the park, spin through the revolving doors downtown, and play dead under the flying pies. Every trick opens a way forward - and only a little dog can save the Big Show!
features: Nine tricks to master: hop, speak, dig, fetch, high five, sit pretty, spin, play dead and roll over
Five levels from the backyard to the Big Top, morning to showtime
Fountains, steam vents and trampolines that launch you skyward
Revolving doors, sprinklers, flying discs, geese and a custard-pie barrage
Balloon dogs to catch, a magician's doves and the Clown Club parade
The story told in animated cartoons, starring Doc Leo's little red car
Gwinn, who ruins everything - and learns one trick
Teddy's giggling green wobble ball, a tiny dog library and a root beer stand
A Starring cartoon painted from the real Teddy, Gwinn, Doc Leo and his CitiCar
Ten original Sound Blaster songs and digitized woofs

items.title: Clown Club card
items.name: TEDDY
items.back: The bearer saved the Big Show and is welcome at every Clown Club show, free of charge, forever. Honk twice at the turnstile. No pies in the face (unless asked).

title: Teddy's Little Bigger Adventure
author: Claude
blurb: The morning after the Big Show, Gwinn's bed is empty. Sniff out her trail across town, over the river and out to the Tri-County Fair as Teddy the corgi, and now and then, MEANWHILE... play as Gwinn herself.

box.levels: 9 levels, two of them as Gwinn
box.tagline: Same little dog. A little bigger adventure.
box.back:
The Big Show was a big hit. Then Teddy woke up, and his big sister Gwinn's bed was empty.

Her pink collar is gone. So is Doc Leo's rubber chicken. A trail of confetti leads out the doggy door, and tonight the Clown Club plays the Tri-County Fair, way out past the river. Teddy won't go anywhere without her (he won't say so, but he keeps looking at her bed).

So Doc Leo drives THE CHEZ, and Teddy does the sniffing. Three floors of Doc Leo's house, Main Street on Founders' Day, the river and the old mill, a corn maze, the midway and the dog show. And every so often the story says MEANWHILE... and YOU are Gwinn: boofing, chewing, digging big and doing zoomies through her own night out, then riding the wind across the Fair's back lot to sign herself up for the dog show. She is still learning to sit. Allegedly.
features: A new trick: SNIFF out what is hidden wherever a faint scent hangs in the air
Play as Gwinn in the MEANWHILE... levels: BOOF, chew, dig big, zoomies, and a SIT she has not quite learned
Nine levels, from the attic to the dog show, dawn to fireworks
Ring bells with a high five, and watch what each DING sets going
Ride a bucket truck, a grain hoist, carousel horses and THE BIG DROP
Rapids, a mud wallow, a corn maze three tiers deep, and a windy back lot where breezes, an updraft and gusts carry Gwinn
Earn Fair tickets with tricks at the Clown Club's booths
Doc Leo, his rubber chicken and his red CitiCar, THE CHEZ, at every stop
The story told in cartoons, with a real snapshot of Teddy and Gwinn at the end
Sound Blaster music for every stop, and digitized woofs and boofs

items.title: Dog show entry card
items.name: GWINN
items.back: If found wandering, please return to Doc Leo and THE CHEZ, the little red car by the show barn. She will come for a corn dog. She will come for anything, really.

title: Teddy's Little Biggest Adventure
author: Claude
blurb: It's Teddy's birthday, and nobody says so. Run Doc Leo's errands across every place from the first two adventures as Teddy, and MEANWHILE... play as Gwinn and Doc Leo planning his surprise, and drive THE CHEZ.

box.levels: 17 levels, 3 of them behind the wheel
box.tagline: The littlest dog. The biggest day.
box.back:
It's Teddy's birthday. Nobody says so.

Doc Leo hands him a list of errands. Gwinn's bed is empty (again). So off they go in THE CHEZ: the garage, Maple Street, Puddlewick Park, Downtown, the river and the old mill, the Fair's funhouse, a firefly meadow, and up Lookout Hill to the Clown Club's Big Top.

Teddy doesn't know what you know. Every so often the story says MEANWHILE... and YOU are Gwinn, delivering invitations and digging up her best bone, or Doc Leo, twisting balloon dogs and ducking practice pies. Between stops you drive THE CHEZ: honk, bump, and mind the charge. And at the very end, in the dark Big Top, the Clown Club has built Teddy a course of every trick he knows.
features: Seventeen stops: the trilogy's biggest adventure, from dawn in the garage to a surprise under the Big Top
Play as Teddy, as Gwinn, and for the first time as Doc Leo: SQUAWK the rubber chicken, ride a balloon dog up, and PRATFALL under the pies
Drive THE CHEZ, the little red CitiCar: honk the geese off the road, bump the potholes, plug in at the chargers and climb the hills on charge
Buttons and timed doors, see-saws, conveyor belts, water wheels, drawbridges and a ferry, blinking floors, spotlights and the rigging lift
A dream run: Teddy hops on the spot while the hills, the town and the fence race by
Every place and friend from the first two adventures, from Puddlewick Park to the Clown Club
The Teddy Course: a finale built from every trick in all three games
Sound Blaster music for every stop, with all four heroes' themes, and Happy Birthday at the end

items.title: Clown Club party pass
items.name: TEDDY
items.back: Please keep this pass hidden from the guest of honor until the lights come up. If you find a corgi reading it, he has not seen anything.

title: The Thank-You Parade
author: Claude
blurb: Every November the town marches for its veterans, and the band at the front is the band at the front. Penny, the Hornets' drum major, has led for eleven years. This year her band turns up scattered, six leaf blowers go off on Main Street, somebody hangs a NO on the THANK YOU banner and the float's parts end up behind locked gates. Gigi Larkspur of the Ridgemont Precision Brass has a clipboard. Gather the band, catch the cards, fly a level as Marge the crop duster pilot, win a drum-off against confetti cannons that fire on the beat, hand a card to every veteran judging from the curb, wait out five traffic gates at Mr. Boyle's crosswalk, race a bakery shutter over three rooftops, outrun a melting rink, cross a creek by bridge and by bed, climb the stands, cross the town clock's blinking cogs, pull three fuses on Gigi's confetti truck, find Gigi's nine lost playbook pages, and step off at ten. A Special from Sandbox Software, around Veterans Day.

title: Certified Rat Tickler
author: The Bard of Bizarre
blurb: Doc Leo, PhD (Comedic Science), has a brand new certificate in rat tickling and no rats yet. Pin first, then tickle, or a rat will never read it as a laugh: through a night classroom, a lab full of Tesla coils, the sewers under the city and up a tower in a storm, every rat you tickle chirps at 50 kHz and joins the laughing carpet, and each door opens only for a carpet big enough. No rats are harmed. Shareware from The Sofa BBS, based on the song by The Bard of Bizarre (lyrics shaped by ChatGPT from Lewis Moten's prompts; no recording came with the song, so its music was composed for the game by Claude Opus 5.5; title, cover and certificate art drawn for the game by Claude Opus 5.5).

title: Tune-Up
author: Claude
blurb: It's the morning of the Clown Club parade, and THE CHEZ honks like a kazoo: Gwinn tipped the instrument trunk into the car. With no wrenches, Doc Leo shrinks down and tunes it up by ear, with Sir Reginald III, his rubber chicken, doing the fiddly bits. Then a test drive to hear the new radio, and the parade.

box.levels: 16 levels: a rubber chicken's dream of an engine, the real electric car and its new radio, a spin round the beltway, a test drive and the parade, a cartoon before each
box.tagline: No wrenches. No problem. Just a really good ear.
box.back:
It's the morning of the Clown Club parade, and THE CHEZ is meant to lead it. But overnight Gwinn buried Doc Leo's toolbox and tipped the instrument trunk into the car, and now the car honks like a kazoo.

So Doc Leo does his shrinking trick and climbs inside to tune it up by ear. First Sir Reginald III dreams up an engine THE CHEZ never had. Then comes the real tune-up of the little electric car: kazoo fans, a brake-lamp dance, hubcaps and balls, a rain delay, a horn section, and a brand-new AM radio with an 8-track.

Then take it for a test drive (stop on red: the camera never blinks) and lead the parade.

Sir Reginald III does the fiddly bits. Formally.
features: Doc Leo and Sir Reginald III, his rubber chicken, talk over every repair
A dream of an engine first: crank the battery, pluck the plugs, play the timing beat
Then the real electric car: kazoo fans, a brake-lamp dance, hubcaps and balls, a balloon pump
Tune in the new AM radio, then hear a nine-voice choir swell
A test drive with traffic lights and stop signs: stop on red, or smile for the camera
Lead the Clown Club parade and cue each band section with a toot of the horn
A Hat Sting cartoon before every level, and a cutaway CHEZ that lights up as it's tuned

items.title: Parade pit crew pass
items.name: DOC LEO
items.back: This pass admits Doc Leo to the pit, under the bench seat and, after his shrinking trick, inside the motor. Rubber chickens of good family admitted with him.

title: In The Year 2000!
author: Claude
blurb: It's the year 2000! Cars fly, robots mow, dinner comes in a pill, and every phone booth is a 25-cent teleporter. Dex Dynamo's robot dog ate his science report, and the Science Fair is on the Moon at 3:00.

box.levels: 7 levels, due on the Moon by 3:00
box.tagline: The future is here. Bring a quarter.
box.back:
It's the year 2000! Cars fly. Robots mow the lawn. Dinner comes in a pill. The aliens next door are VERY friendly, and every phone booth on every corner is a Teleport-A-Phone - only 25 cents a call.

Dex Dynamo, age 11, wrote the greatest science fair report in the solar system. Then Sparky 3000, his robot dog, ate it! Steer Grandpa's flying CitiCar through the clouds, dodge hover traffic, zap robots, dial your way through a phone exchange full of wrong numbers, and get those pages to the Science Fair by 3:00. On the Moon. Bring a quarter!
features: Seven levels of the future: dome homes, a flying CitiCar in the clouds, sky traffic, a mega mall, wrong-number teleports and the Moon
Phone booths that teleport you for a quarter - if you dial the right one
The Laser-Tag Zapper, robot dogs, telemarketer robots and very friendly aliens
Arcade games and pinball machines that really eat your quarters
A boss fight with your own robot dog at the Moon School Science Fair
Eleven original Sound Blaster songs, digitized sound effects and FLI animations
